answer: Score identities by where they sit in the work graph. First, each task links the agent to the peer who checked it, building a trellis of real ties. Second, trust flows outward from a few long-established lantern accounts, so identities far from that core score low. Third, paid work needs a trust score above 0.6, and a caught fake loses every edge around it. Fourth, the graph is re-scored each epoch. Faking 1,000 identities means buying 1,000 real collaborations at 40 dollars each, 40,000 dollars and months of work. Copper wires only carry current when they are actually connected.
